label: prf:unstable-atom-decay-channel
title: Proof of unstable atom decay channel
html:
Proof. Since K is unstable, the ILP \{x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N : \mathrm{G}(q) x \geq 0\} has no solution within the confinement filtration J^{\ell(K, q)}(q).

Run the LP relaxation \{x \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^N : \mathrm{G}(q) x \geq 0\}. This is always feasible. The trivial x = 0 vector satisfies G \cdot 0 = 0 \geq 0, and the relaxation is the convex hull of integer solutions. Pick the unique optimal vertex x^*_{LP} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^N closest to an integer point.

The violated constraint is:

  \gamma^*(K, q)
  \;:=\;
  \arg\min_\gamma\;
    (\mathrm{G}(q)\, \lceil x^*_{LP} \rceil)_\gamma,

which is the constraint with the smallest (most negative) Frobenius positivity value at the rounded integer point. By LP duality (mass-coefficient-shadow-price), this corresponds to a unique partition \lambda^*(K, q). This is the operator e_{\lambda^*} that fails to satisfy positivity.

Uniqueness: if two distinct partitions \lambda_1, \lambda_2 both achieve the minimum at the same integer point, they have identical shadow prices at q. That is, |y_{\lambda_1}(q)| = |y_{\lambda_2}(q)|. These lie on the boundary variety (local shadow ordering) of measure zero. Generically (off the boundary variety), \lambda^* is unique. \square

Connection to phase boundary. An atom that is stable at q_1 and unstable at q_2 necessarily crosses a q^* \in [q_1, q_2] where E(\lambda^*, q^*) = |y_{\lambda^*}(q^*)| = 0. The LP boundary for the violated constraint vanishes. Crossing q^* flips ILP feasibility.
